trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident that affects a covered contractor information system or the covered defense information in it, including the CEE gateway
deadline: Within 72 hours of discovery. Report what is known; add updates as the review continues
notify: DoD at https://dibnet.dod.mil with a DoD-approved medium assurance certificate (252.204-7012(c)(3))
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - prime contractor and subcontractor; 4 certificate holders

obligation: Review for compromise of covered defense information
trigger: Same trigger as the DoD report
deadline: Starts at discovery; results feed the report and its updates
notify: Internal (results go to DoD in the report)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - identify compromised computers, servers, specific data, and user accounts, including other systems that may have been accessed

obligation: Incident report number to each higher-tier contractor
trigger: DoD assigns an incident report number after the DIBNet report
deadline: As soon as practicable
notify: Prime A to Prime D, for CUI that belongs to their subcontracts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the company is a subcontractor on Prime A to Prime D programs
clock_starts: Receipt of the DoD incident report number

obligation: Supplier reports to the company (company as higher tier)
trigger: A supplier reports a cyber incident involving the company CUI it holds
deadline: Supplier gives the incident report number as soon as practicable
notify: Company CMMC Program Office (supplier incident intake)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - for the 380 CUI suppliers; check whether the company also has a reporting duty for its own systems

trigger: Malicious software discovered and isolated in connection with a reported incident
deadline: As instructed by DC3 or the contracting officer; never to the contracting officer
notify: DoD Cyber Crime Center (DC3)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - a web shell or loader on the gateway is expected in this scenario

trigger: Discovery of a cyber incident
deadline: At least 90 days from submission of the DIBNet report, so DoD can request the media or decline interest
notify: Internal custody; forensic retainer; cloud provider
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - images of the gateway VMs, web application firewall and network logs, packet capture

obligation: DoD access for forensic analysis and damage assessment
trigger: DoD request for more information or equipment; contracting officer request for damage assessment information
deadline: On request
notify: DoD (through the contracting officer)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the Vice President, Contracts is the DoD liaison

trigger: Incident involving CUI in the government-community cloud
deadline: Provider must comply with paragraphs (c) to (g); coordinate so reports and preserved data match
notify: Government-community cloud provider (security contact from the CRM)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the gateway runs in the government-community subscription

obligation: Cleared contractor cyber incident report (classified system)
trigger: Cyber incident on a classified covered information system approved by DCSA
deadline: Immediately
notify: DoD cognizant security office (DCSA)
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the classified system at FL-1 is affected. Not expected: it is stand-alone

obligation: Cleared contractor reports on unclassified systems
trigger: Cyber incident on non-Federal unclassified systems
deadline: In accordance with contract requirements (here, the DFARS 252.204-7012 report)
notify: DoD through DIBNet
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - satisfied by the DIBNet report

trigger: Efforts by any individual to obtain unauthorized access to classified information or the cleared facility, including targeting of cleared employees
deadline: As required by DCSA guidance
notify: DCSA
applies_at_this_tier: Assess - if the actor targeted cleared employees or Program K data

trigger: Senior Empowered Official believes an ITAR violation may have occurred
deadline: Voluntary. Initial notification immediately after discovery; full disclosure within 60 calendar days of the notification unless an extension is granted
notify: Directorate of Defense Trade Controls
applies_at_this_tier: Decision by the Senior Empowered Official with export counsel. Theft by an outside attacker may not be a company violation; document the reasoning either way

trigger: Company believes it may have violated the EAR (commercial program technology)
deadline: Voluntary; a deliberate decision not to disclose a significant apparent violation is an aggravating factor (764.5(a))
notify: BIS Office of Export Enforcement
applies_at_this_tier: Decision by the Vice President, Trade Compliance with export counsel

trigger: Cybersecurity incident discovered that could be material
deadline: Without unreasonable delay after discovery (the disclosure committee convenes within 48 hours under POL-03 4.4)
notify: Disclosure committee (General Counsel chairs); record the date and time of the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

trigger: Registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: Within 4 business days after the materiality determination
notify: SEC (public filing): material aspects of the nature, scope, and timing, and the material impact or reasonably likely material impact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant. The draft must not include CUI, export-controlled, or classified details (company content review step)

obligation: SEC filing delay on Attorney General determination
trigger: U.S. Attorney General determines disclosure poses a substantial risk to national security or public safety and notifies the SEC in writing
deadline: Up to 30 days after the original due date; up to 30 more days on a further determination; in extraordinary circumstances a final period of up to 60 days (national security only)
notify: Department of Justice (through outside counsel); SEC notified by the Attorney General
applies_at_this_tier: Possible - a state-sponsored theft of defense program data may raise national security questions; request through outside counsel

trigger: Annual report on Form 10-K
deadline: With the next Form 10-K; update the description of processes and of any material effects of incidents
notify: SEC (Form 10-K)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - SEC registrant

obligation: State breach notice to individuals (each state of residence)
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam)
trigger: Breach of personal information of residents, as each state defines it
deadline: Varies by state: some say without unreasonable delay; some set a fixed number of days
notify: Affected residents of each state (here, employees whose payroll files were on the corporate file transfer instance)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside; counsel state matrix
clock_starts: Varies by state (often determination of a breach)

obligation: State attorney general or regulator notice
trigger: Breach above a state-set count of residents, or any breach in some states
deadline: Varies by state
notify: State attorney general or other designated regulator
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state requires

trigger: Notices above a state-set count
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes where the state threshold is met

trigger: Breach of security of personal information of Florida residents
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination of a breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (law enforcement delay under 501.171(4)(b); 15 more days on written good cause under 501.171(3)(a) for this notice only)
notify: Affected Florida residents by mail or email
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Florida employees in the payroll files
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred
owner: Chief Human Resources Officer with the General Counsel

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 30 days after determination (the 15-day good-cause extension applies only to notice to individuals)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (synopsis, count, services offered, copy of notice, contact)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more Florida residents
clock_starts: Determination of the breach or reason to believe one occurred

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, content of notices)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if more than 1,000

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the company (worked example)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by a vendor acting as third-party agent
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and no later than 10 days after the agent determines the breach
notify: The company
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the incident started at a vendor (for example, the payroll SaaS)

trigger: Incident affecting a customer program or deliveries
deadline: Per contract (often 72 hours or sooner)
notify: DoD contracting officers; Prime A to Prime D security contacts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - check each contract; coordinate with the DIBNet report

trigger: Incident affecting SL-1 or SL-2 customer data
deadline: Per agreement
notify: MRO and analytics customers
applies_at_this_tier: Only if SL-1 or SL-2 data is affected (not expected; separate cloud)

trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy (call the carrier hotline before hiring vendors)
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Contractual

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any extortion payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (2021-09-21); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Any payment to an extortionist is considered
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license request if a sanctioned party is involved); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Only if extortion occurs. Payment needs CEO, General Counsel, and insurer approval (POL-03 4.7)

trigger: Suspected theft of controlled technical information by a foreign or criminal actor
deadline: As soon as practical; coordinate with the DIBNet report
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Recommended

citation: FAR 52.204-25(d); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Discovery of covered telecommunications equipment or services during contract performance
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification; mitigation details within 10 business days. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer (DoD: https://dibnet.dod.mil)
applies_at_this_tier: No - not triggered by this incident type

obligation: CIRCIA incident and ransom payment reports (PROPOSED)
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours; 24 hours after a ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: No - final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; not a current obligation
